editorial_note: Corrected against the pinned VishvAsa/Vasuki Śrīdhara Svāmī source. Each Sanskrit block now matches the source block for its range; each English literal and word-for-word pair translates that block only. The source explicitly has no Śrīdhara commentary only at 3.17.24.

entries.sanskrit:
ततः सप्तदशे जन्म तयोर् लोक-भयङ्-करम् ।

हिरण्याक्ष-प्रभावश् च वर्ण्यते दिग्-जयेऽद्भुतः ॥

क्षेमं विधास्यति [३.१६.३७] इति ब्रह्म-वचनानन्तरं । शङ्कया त्यक्ताः ॥१॥
pairs: after Brahmā’s statement, “Thus, he will bring welfare”
was abandoned; they gave it up
entries.literal_english: Then, in the seventeenth chapter, the birth of the two—terrifying to the worlds—and the wondrous prowess of Hiraṇyākṣa in conquering the directions are described. After Brahmā’s statement, “He will bring welfare” (3.16.37), they gave up their apprehension.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: भर्तुर् आदेशात् लोकान् स-पालांस् त्रींश् चण्डि मुहुर् आक्रन्दयिष्यतः [भा।पु। ३.१४.३९] इति वाक्यात् । स्वापत्याभ्यां परिशङ्किनी देवोपद्रवं शङ्कमाना ॥२॥
pairs: the three worlds together with their protectors
they will make [them] cry out repeatedly
entries.literal_english: Because of her husband’s statement, “O fierce one, they will repeatedly make the three worlds together with their protectors cry out” (Bhāg. 3.14.39), she was apprehensive about her own two children, fearing that they would bring trouble to the gods.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: तत्र तदा निपेतुर् उद्बभूवुः । उरु भयम् आसमन्ताद् वहन्तीति ॥३॥
entries.literal_english: They appeared there and then, carrying great fear all around.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: अचलैः सहिता भुवः प्रदेशाः । केतवश् चोदयां चक्रुर् इति शेषः ॥४॥
pairs: the regions of the earth together with the mountains
and [the sense] ‘rose’ is to be supplied
entries.literal_english: “Acalaiḥ sahitā bhuvaḥ” means the regions of the earth together with the mountains. With “comets,” the sense “rose” is to be supplied.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: फूत्-कारान् इति तीव्र-वायु-शब्दानुकरणम् । नग-पतीन् महा-वृक्षान् । वात्या एव अनीकं यस्य । रज एव ध्वजो यस्य ॥५॥
pairs: imitates the sound of a fierce wind
entries.literal_english: “Phūt-kāra” imitates the sound of a fierce wind. “Lords of trees” means great trees. Whirlwinds were his army, and dust was his banner.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: उच्चैर् हसन्त्य इव तडितो येषु तेषाम् अम्बुदानां घटया समूहेन नष्टो भा-गणः सूर्यादि-प्रभा-समूहो यस्मिन् । पदं स्थानं न व्यादृश्यते स्म ईषद् अपि नादृश्यत ॥६॥
pairs: lightning flashes as if laughing loudly
of those clouds in which [lightning flashed]
the host of lights was obscured
the aggregate of lights such as the sun
it could not be seen even a little
entries.literal_english: The lightning flashes in those clouds seemed to laugh aloud. By the mass of those clouds, the host of lights—such as the sun—was obscured, so that no place could be made out, even slightly.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: वार्धिः समुद्रो विमना इव । उद्गता ऊर्मयो यस्मात् । क्षुभिता उदर-स्था मकरादयो यस्मिन् । उदपानैर् वापी-कूपादिभिः सहिताः । शुष्काणि पङ्कजानि यासु ॥७॥
pairs: in which makaras and other creatures in its belly were agitated
with tanks, wells, and the like
together with ponds, wells, and so forth
in which the lotuses had dried up
entries.literal_english: The ocean seemed dismayed. Its waves had risen, and the makaras and other creatures in its belly were agitated. The reservoirs, tanks, wells, and the like had lotuses that were dried up.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: परिधयः परिवेषाः । स-राह्वो राहु-ग्रस्तयोः । निर्घाता निरभ्र-गर्जितानि । रथ-निर्ह्राद-तुल्या ध्वनयः । विवरेभ्यो गिरि-गुहाभ्यः ॥८॥
pairs: of [the sun and moon] together with Rāhu / seized by Rāhu
of the two eclipsed by Rāhu
sounds like the rumble of chariots
entries.literal_english: Halos appeared; the sun and moon were seized by Rāhu. There were cloudless thunderclaps, and sounds like the rumbling of chariots came from the mountain caves.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: सृगालानाम् उलूकानां च टङ्कारैर् ध्वनिभिः सह । शिवाः सृगाल्यः ॥९॥
entries.literal_english: There were the cries of jackals and owls; “śivāḥ” means female jackals.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.literal_english: “Village-lions” means dogs.
entries.source_note: The pinned source prints this short gloss jointly under Śrīdhara Svāmī and Viśvanātha Cakravartī; the shared gloss is identical.

entries.sanskrit: कर्कशैस् तीक्ष्णैः । हे क्षत्तः ! खार्कारो गर्दभ-जाति-शब्दस् तस्मिन् रभसः संभ्रमो येषाम् । वरूथशः सङ्घशः ॥११॥
pairs: the sound of the donkey kind
and confusion in those [who heard it]
entries.literal_english: “Harsh” means piercing. O Kṣattṛ! “Khārkāra” is the sound characteristic of donkeys; those who heard it were thrown into agitation and confusion, in groups.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: रासभ-शब्दात् त्रस्ताः सर्वतः क्रोशन्तः ॥१२॥
entries.literal_english: Frightened by the donkeys’ cries, they shouted on every side.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: गावोऽत्रसन् त्रस्ताः । असृग् दोहाश् च बभूवुः । देव-लिङ्गानि व्यरुदन्, प्रतिमानाम् अश्रु-स्राव आसीद् इत्य् अर्थः ॥१३॥
pairs: the images of the gods wept
the meaning is that tears flowed from the images
entries.literal_english: The cows trembled with fear. They became blood-yielders. “The images of the gods wept” means that tears flowed from the images.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: पुण्यतमान् गुरु-बुधादीन् भ-गणान् बहूनि नक्षत्राणि च, अन्ये क्रूर-ग्रहा मङ्गलादयोऽतिचेरुर् अतिक्रम्य जग्मुर् वक्र-गत्या प्रत्यावृत्य युयुधुश् च ॥१४॥
entries.literal_english: The highly auspicious celestial bodies, such as Jupiter and Mercury, along with many constellations, were passed over by other malefic planets, such as Mars; they went past, turned back in retrograde motion, and contended with them.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: ब्रह्म-पुत्रान् ऋते विना, तेषां स्व-शापादि-ज्ञानात् ॥१५॥
pairs: because of knowledge of their own curses and related matters
entries.literal_english: Except for Brahmā’s sons, because of their knowledge of their own curses and related matters.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: व्यज्यमानम् आत्म-पौरुषं पूर्व-सिद्धं स्व-पौरुषं ययोः ॥१६॥
pairs: the own prowess of the two
entries.literal_english: The prowess of the two, already established beforehand, was becoming manifest.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: निरुद्धा व्याप्ताः काष्ठा दिशो याभ्याम् । स्फुरन्त्य् अङ्गदानि येषु ते भुजा ययोः। अङ्गदेति टाब्-अन्तत्वम् आर्षम् । शोभना काञ्ची यस्यां तया कट्या ॥१७॥
pairs: the feminine ending ṭāp in ‘aṅgadā’ is an archaic usage
entries.literal_english: The directions were filled by the two. Their armlets gleamed on their arms. The ending in ṭāp in the form “aṅgadā” is an archaic usage. A beautiful girdle adorned the waist.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit:
यमयोर् मध्ये यः स्व-देहात् प्रथमम् अजायत, तं यथा हिरण्यकशिपुं विदुः । सा दितिः प्रथमं यम् असूत, तं हिरण्याक्षं यथा विदुस् तथा नाम कृतवान् इत्य् अर्थः । अयं भावः---यदा हि गर्भाधान-समये योनि-पुष्पं विशद्-वीर्यं द्विधा विभक्तम् आदि-पश्चाद्-भावेन प्रविशति, तदा यमौ भवतः । तयोश् च पितृतः प्रवेश-क्रम-विपर्ययेण मातृतः प्रसूतिः ।
यदा विशेद् द्विधा-भूतं बीजं पुष्पं परिक्षरत् ।
द्वौ तदा भवतो गर्भौ सूतिर् वेश-विपर्ययात् ॥ इति  पिण्ड-सिद्धि-स्मरणात् ।

अतः स्व-देहात् पूर्वं यो जातस् तस्य हिरण्यकशिपुर् इति दितिः प्रथमं यम् असूत तस्य हिरण्याक्ष इति नाम कृतवान् इति ॥१८॥
pairs: the one who was born first from her body
the one whom she bore first
this is the meaning: she gave the names in that way
the order of entry from the father being reversed
is the birth from the mother
the seed that has become twofold
birth occurs in the reverse order of entry
the one born first from her body
the one whom Diti bore first
she gave him the name Hiraṇyākṣa
entries.literal_english: Among the twins, the one who was born first from her body was known as Hiraṇyakaśipu; the one whom Diti delivered first was known as Hiraṇyākṣa. That is, she gave them those names respectively. The point is this: when, at conception, the seed enters the womb-flower divided in two, in an order of first and later, twins result. Their birth from the mother takes place in the reverse order of their entry from the father. As the Piṇḍa-siddhi is recalled: “When the seed, divided in two, enters the flower, two embryos then arise; birth occurs in the reverse order of entry.” Therefore the one born first from her body was named Hiraṇyakaśipu, while Diti gave the name Hiraṇyākṣa to the one she delivered first.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: दोर्भ्याम् उद्धतो ब्रह्म-वरेणाकुतो-मृत्युः ॥१९॥
pairs: one for whom death could come from nowhere
entries.literal_english: He was made arrogant by the strength of his arms; because of Brahmā’s boon, he was one for whom death could come from nowhere.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: रणं युद्धम् ॥२०॥
entries.literal_english: “Raṇam” means battle.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: दुःसहो जवो वेगो यस्य । रणन्तौ काञ्चन-मयौ नूपुरौ यस्य । अंसे न्यस्ता महती गदा येन ॥२१॥ मनसा शौर्येण वीर्येण बलेन वरेण च उत्सिक्तं गर्वितम् । असृण्यं निरङ्कुशम् । निलिल्यिरे लीना बभूवुः ॥२२॥
pairs: whose speed was hard to withstand
entries.literal_english: His speed was hard to withstand; his two golden anklets rang, and a great mace was placed on his shoulder.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: स्वेन महसा तेजसा तिरोहितान् स दृष्ट्वा ज्ञात्वा क्षीबान् मत्तान् अपश्यन् सन् । "क्लीबान्" इति पाठे पौरुष-हीनान् ॥२३॥
pairs: being unable to see / find them
entries.literal_english: Seeing, that is, understanding, that they had been hidden by his own radiance, he did not find the intoxicated gods. On the reading “klībān,” it means “lacking manliness.”
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: The pinned source explicitly marks 3.17.24 as “न व्याख्यातम्।” This is a no-commentary range, not a missing-source gap.

entries.sanskrit: सन्ना अवसन्ना धीर् येषाम् । वर्चसा तेजसा प्रघर्षिता अभिभूताः सन्तः ॥२५॥
entries.literal_english: Their minds were dejected and collapsed. Being overpowered by his radiance, they were subdued.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: महोर्मीन् अभिजघ्ने । मौर्व्या मारयतीति मौर्वं कार्ष्णायसं तन्-मय्या । यद् वा, मूर्वा नाम तृण-विशेषः, तन्-मय-रज्ज्वा दृढ-निबद्धयेत्य् अर्थः । विभावरी-संज्ञाम् आसेदिवान् प्राप्तः ॥२६॥
pairs: mūrvā is the name of a particular grass
with a cord made from it
entries.literal_english: He struck the great waves with the maurvī. “Maurva” is black iron, described as that which kills; [he struck them] with one made of it. Alternatively, mūrvā is a particular kind of grass; the meaning is ‘with a rope made from it, firmly bound.’ He reached the city called Vibhāvarī.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: असुराणां लोकः पातालं, तत्-पालकम् । प्रलब्धुम् उपहसितुं प्रणिपत्य ॥२७॥
entries.literal_english: “The world of the asuras” means Pātāla, and [Hiraṇyākṣa was] its protector. He bowed down in order to mock and ridicule [it].
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: यद् यस्माद् राजसूये भवान् अयजत् ॥२८॥
entries.literal_english: “Yat” means “because”: because you performed the Rājasūya sacrifice.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: उपशमं युद्धादि-कौतुकाद् उपरमम् ॥२९॥
pairs: from the sport of war and the like
entries.literal_english: “Upaśama” means cessation from the sport of war and the like.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: युद्ध-मार्ग-निपुणं त्वां यस् तोषयिष्यति तम् इहि गच्छ । गृणते स्तुवन्ति ॥३०॥
pairs: skilled in the ways of battle
entries.literal_english: Go to him—the one who will satisfy you, skilled in the ways of battle. “Gṛṇate” means “they praise.”
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: आराच् छीघ्रम् । विस्मयो नष्ट-गर्वः । वीरशये रणाङ्गणे । रूपाणि वराहाद्य्-अवतारान् ॥३१॥
pairs: one whose pride has been destroyed
entries.literal_english: “Ārāt” means soon. “Chīghram” means quickly. “Vismaya” means [one whose] pride has been destroyed. “Vīraśaya” means the battlefield, where heroes lie. “Forms” means incarnations beginning with Varāha.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.
